summary: This Vedantu study page compares sperm and ovum, the male and female gametes of human reproduction. It describes each cell's definition, structure, production and function, then gives a comparison table covering motility, size, chromosomes, centrioles and formation. The page also has an FAQ on fertilisation, sex chromosomes, semen, unfertilised ova and artificial insemination.
one_line: A study guide contrasting sperm and ovum, the male and female gametes, covering their structure, production, chromosomes and role in fertilisation.
key_facts: Sperm is the male gamete, and a human sperm cell is haploid with 23 chromosomes.
Sperm is stored in the epididymis and released from the penis during ejaculation along with a fluid called semen.
The sperm head contains a nucleus with densely coiled chromatin fibres and an acrosome containing enzymes that help penetration into the egg.
The sperm tail, also called the flagellum, is the longest part of a sperm and moves in a wave-like motion.
Ovum, also called the egg cell or ova in plural, is the female gamete and is non-motile.
An ovum in humans measures approximately 0.1 mm in diameter and is visible to the naked eye without a microscope.
Ovum structure includes ooplasm containing a germinal vesicle (nucleus) and a germinal spot (nucleolus), plus formative yolk and nutritive yolk.
Sperms are produced in the testes, while ova are produced in the ovary.
One spermatogonium results in the formation of four sperms, while one oogonium results in only one ovum.
Sperm cells contain X or Y chromosomes, while egg cells contain only X chromosomes.
The page states that the human ovum is one of the largest cells in the body and that sperm are the smallest cells in the human body.
The page states that the male ejaculation fluid semen contains sperm only about 2-3% of its volume, with the whole volume usually 2-3 ml.
An unfertilised ovum waits for sperm in the fallopian tube for around one day before being carried to the uterus by cilia and discharged through the vagina.

Human sperm are formed by spermatogenesis in the seminiferous tubules of the testes, and an ovum is released on a cycled basis, with one ovum released by both ovaries on an alternate basis in the mid-day of the menstrual cycle.
Artificial insemination is described as the deliberate introduction of sperm into a female's uterine cavity or cervix to achieve pregnancy.

entities.name: Vedantu
entities.role: Online learning platform that published the study page and offers the FAQs and related study material

entities.name: NCERT
entities.role: Educational body whose Class 12 Biology solutions and notes are linked on the page

entities.name: Human sperm
entities.role: Male gamete, haploid with 23 chromosomes, that joins the female ovum to form a diploid cell

entities.name: Ovum
entities.role: Female gamete, non-motile egg cell that is fertilised by sperm to form a zygote

entities.name: Acrosome
entities.role: Thin flattened sac covering the sperm head that contains enzymes for penetrating the egg

entities.name: Flagellum
entities.role: Tail of the sperm that enables swimming and penetration of the egg

entities.name: Semen
entities.role: Fluid released with sperm during ejaculation that nurtures and transports sperm

entities.name: Testes
entities.role: Male reproductive organ where sperm are produced in the seminiferous tubules

entities.name: Ovary
entities.role: Female reproductive organ that forms and releases the ovum

entities.name: Fallopian tube
entities.role: Site where the ovum waits for sperm to arrive and fertilisation to occur

entities.name: Zygote
entities.role: Diploid cell formed when sperm and ovum fuse, which can grow into a new organism

entities.name: Artificial insemination
entities.role: Deliberate introduction of sperm into a female's uterine cavity or cervix to achieve pregnancy
